evidence: Public Enemy's 'Bring the Noise' (1987) samples Funkadelic's 'Get Off Your Ass and Jam' (1975), as documented on WhoSampled and in liner/production breakdowns of 'It Takes a Nation of Millions to Hold Us Back'. The Bomb Squad drew on Parliament-Funkadelic material across multiple Public Enemy records of the period.

earlier.title: Get Off Your Ass and Jam

trackPair.whatToListenFor: Funkadelic's original is a loose, live-sounding jam built to fill a dance floor. The Bomb Squad chops it into a hard, repeating stab buried under sirens, scratches and Chuck D's vocal, the same move e-jamesbrown-publicenemy describes with 'Funky Drummer': the source record's groove becomes raw material for something faster, louder and more urgent.

explanation: 'Bring the Noise' (1987) samples Funkadelic's 'Get Off Your Ass and Jam' (1975). The Bomb Squad, Public Enemy's production team, treated P-Funk's records the same way they treated James Brown's: as raw material for a dense, aggressive new sound. Those two catalogues are the Bomb Squad's biggest funk sources, and 'Bring the Noise' is one of several Public Enemy records built partly from Parliament-Funkadelic.
